title: Least-recently-used cache
prompt:
Design a fixed-capacity key-value cache that, when full, evicts the entry that was used least recently, with get and put both running in O(1) time.

- Implement the class LruCache(capacity) with get(key) and put(key, value). The driver runLruCache(capacity, ops) is already written: ops looks like [["put", 1, 10], ["get", 1]] and it returns one output per op (null/None for "put").
- get(key) returns the stored value, or -1 if the key is not in the cache. A successful get counts as a use.
- put(key, value) inserts or overwrites the value and counts as a use. If the key is new and the cache already holds capacity entries, first remove the least recently used entry.
- capacity is 1 to 10,000; keys are integers; values are integers from 0 to 10^9; up to 100,000 ops.
hints: You need O(1) lookup by key and O(1) access to the oldest-used entry. Which two structures give you each of those?
Combine a hash map with a list ordered by last use; every get or put moves the key to the "most recent" end.
On put of a new key when full, remove the key at the "least recent" end, then insert. A doubly linked list (or an insertion-ordered map) makes move and remove O(1).

solution.explanation: A hash map finds entries in O(1); keeping them in recency order lets the oldest be evicted in O(1). JavaScript Map and Python OrderedDict both preserve insertion order, so re-inserting (or move_to_end) on each use keeps the least recently used key at the front. Interviewers often ask for the underlying structure: a hash map from key to node in a doubly linked list.

complexity.notes: Map and OrderedDict give O(1) average time because they are hash tables threaded with a linked list, exactly the structure you would build by hand.

followUps: Implement it without Map/OrderedDict ordering, using your own doubly linked list with sentinel nodes.
How would you make this cache safe to use from many threads, and where is the contention?
